upstream.description: Shared memory for your team's coding agents

classification.analysis: Stash is a self-hostable 'shared memory' platform for teams of coding agents: it automatically streams Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/etc. session transcripts, connects to sources like GitHub, Gmail, Drive, Slack, Notion, Linear, and Jira, and exposes everything to agents via a CLI, ~70-tool MCP server, REST API, and a virtual filesystem shell. A scheduled 'curator' agent compiles new sessions and files into a linked wiki of entities and concepts, and Skills (folders with a SKILL.md) can be published, forked, or auto-installed into other agents' setups. It targets engineering teams and solo builders who want persistent, cross-session context so coding agents stop duplicating prior work, and ships as a Python/TypeScript backend+frontend with a Docker Compose self-hosted deployment.

use_cases.title: Give a team's coding agents shared, persistent memory across sessions
Expose GitHub, Slack, Notion, and Gmail to an agent via one MCP server
Auto-generate a wiki of entities and decisions from past agent sessions
Publish and install reusable Skills across a team's agents
